reviews.text: Here me out- the concept of the movie is amazing. I understand, empathize and relate to Barry as a character and would've LOVED to see him open up and be comfortable with being vulnerable and being seen through therapy or getting help from friends and family (boy had 7 sisters). The music helps us understand his perspective and how easily he can get overwhelmed by people around him. Instead of turning it towards a pointless romance, it would have been better if it revolved around Barry and his relationships with the people already present in his life. The romance between both protagonist seemed absolutely ingenuine and you CANNOT convince me otherwise. This is the most horrifying rom com I've ever seen. I couldn't let go of the idea that one day, Barry might end up hurting Lena too, in his fit of rage. As much as I love Love, it simply is not enough to change the whole inner and psychological dynamics of a person who has spent their whole life being one way. That being said, I respect those who liked this movie but it simply wasn't for me

I usually like Adam Sandler movies that were written and directed by someone else, like Uncut Gems or Meyerowitz stories, but this movie was honestly really weird and I mean that in a bad way. I get that it's trying to show us some sort of inside image of a deeply insecure man with 7 sisters that all make fun of him relentlessly and don't give a single fuck about his feelings. That on it's own is bizarre, but not nearly as bizarre as every single event in this movie. Nothing makes any fucking sense. There are multiple car crashes that kind of don't matter, especially the one at the start of the movie. None of the things happen in a logical chronological order, which is funny cause if you watch the trailer for this movie, they have it edited in a way that makes a lot more sense than the chronology of these events in the movie. I give it one extra star for Gail the Snail. Otherwise, it's horrible, and I have found a new distrust for everyone that says this movie is a masterpiece. What the actual fuck do you guys mean?

Barry Egan will, without question, be physically and verbally abusive to Lena over the course of their relationship, even if he really does love her. Everything we learn about Barry, from how he treats his sisters to his pathological lying to his general inability to control his emotions, points toward this. He is violent, unstable and untrustworthy—and love, for all its beauty, is a turbulent force, not a calming one. Self-control is exactly what it sounds like: it comes from the self , not from a lover. Barry's "quirky" traits would be entirely forgivably from a character standpoint if he recognized his own flaws and made any attempt to improve or mature in ways that really matter. Telling someone you want to stop crying all the time and telling someone you want to stop lying all the time are two different things, and Barry is only interested in the former. The credits rolled and all I felt was scared for Lena, a character whose sole narrative purpose is to inexplicably love Barry. Really not trying to be annoyingly contrarian here, but this was just a tough first watch in 2026. I can see why it was important to so many oddballs, introverts, quiet creative types and whatnot back in the day. Seeing a version of your own weirdness depicted, victorious, and loved is, I imagine, very affirming. But I am baffled by how many people I know identify with Barry. He simply does not deserve the good things happening to him. I want to believe that if you made this movie today, it would be broadly rejected. Undeniably beautiful filmmaking, though. Shitty L.A. never looked better. But no.
